sections.h2: Where are Washington County property records kept?
sections.html:
The Washington County Clerk records deeds and other real property documents at 100 East Main Street, Suite 102, in Brenham. The county's own welcome page calls Washington County "the Birth Place of Texas."

In Texas the county clerk is the county recorder, and instruments that affect land are filed with the clerk of the county the land lies in. A deed for a house in Chappell Hill, Burton, Independence or Gay Hill goes to the same Brenham office as a deed for a house in Brenham itself. Those community names appear in the Texas State Library's list of the county's old justice precinct records, which is a handy reminder of how the county is divided.

The clerk's page lists 979-277-6216 for appointments, so call that number to ask about hours, walk-in service and anything the website does not cover. The clerk's office also keeps probate filings, foreclosure notices posted for sale and, under Texas law, notices of state tax liens.

  • Deeds, deeds of trust, releases, affidavits, leases and powers of attorney: County Clerk, Brenham.
  • Appraisal values and exemptions: the county appraisal district.
  • Tax certificates and tax bills: the county tax office.

sections.h2: How do I search Washington County deed records online?
sections.html:
The clerk's recording page says Official Public Records are available online through eDocTec, and that deed records and official public records are online from 1836 to the present. Use the index to find an instrument, then ask the clerk about copies.

Records from before the modern index exist in other forms too. The Texas State Library lists the county's deed record for 1834 to 1904 on microfilm held at Texas A&M University in College Station, with direct and reverse indexes on separate reels. The same list covers probate minutes, probate records, marriage records from 1837 and tax rolls from 1837 to 1910. A title examiner usually works backward through these books, and a seller with an old family farm may need that chain of title when a buyer's title company asks for it.

  • Start with the owner's name and the most recent deed, then follow the deed of trust and any release.
  • Look for liens, easements and affidavits recorded after the deed.
  • For a plat, ask the clerk for a copy; the county lists $10.00 for a plat copy.
  • For an inherited house, look for a recorded transfer on death deed, a muniment of title order or an affidavit of heirship.

sections.h2: What are the Washington County Clerk's recording fees?
sections.html:
The county's recording page lists $25.00 for the first page of a document and $4.00 for each additional page. After five names, indexing adds $0.25 per name.

Washington County Clerk recording fees as printed on the county's recording page
ItemFee printed by the county
Recording, first page$25.00
Each additional page$4.00
Each name indexed after five$0.25
Federal tax lien or release, IRS$30.00 each
Filing a plat$70.00 per slide
Copy of a plat$10.00

Source: Washington County Clerk recording page. The state county clerk manual (2023 edition) describes the statutory structure differently: a first-page fee of $5.00, $4.00 for each added page, a records management fee of up to $10, a records archive fee of up to $10 and a $2.00 records technology fee. Ask the clerk for the exact total on your document before you mail it, because the clerk's page and the manual do not break the fees down the same way.

Mail documents to the Washington County Clerk, 100 East Main Street, Suite 102, Brenham, TX 77833, with the correct filing fee. The county also notes that a plat needs a current tax certificate showing no delinquent ad valorem taxes.

sections.h2: What must a deed have to be recorded in Washington County?
sections.html:
A deed must be an original, properly notarized or certified by the recording office of another county, state or country. The clerk's page adds that documents must meet any requirements set out in Texas statute.

Texas Property Code section 12.001(b), as summarized in the state clerk manual, allows an instrument conveying real property to be recorded only if it is signed and acknowledged or sworn to before two subscribing witnesses or before an officer authorized to take acknowledgments, such as a notary or a clerk. The manual lists the kinds of deed records a county clerk takes: general warranty deeds, special warranty deeds, quitclaim deeds, trustee's deeds, sheriff's deeds, tax deeds, affidavits, releases of deeds of trust, leases, contracts of sale and powers of attorney. A missing grantee mailing address on a deed can add a $25 charge under the manual.

  • Use the original signed document, not a photocopy.
  • Have the signature acknowledged before a notary or other authorized officer.
  • Include the grantee's mailing address.
  • Send the fee for the first page, added pages and any extra names.

The commissioners court may direct the clerk to waive real property recording fees for buyers using certain federal or state grant programs. Ask whether Washington County has done so for your program.

sections.h2: How do inheritance and probate filings show up in Washington County records?
sections.html:
They appear as recorded instruments that connect the owner on the old deed to the heirs. Which instrument you need depends on whether the estate went through court.

The State Law Library lists the routes. A transfer on death deed passes real property without probate but must be recorded before the owner's death, in the county of the land. A muniment of title lets a will pass title without full administration, and the court order and will are filed with the clerk of the county the land is in. A small estate affidavit under Estates Code chapter 205 applies to estates of $75,000 or less, excluding the homestead and exempt property, and requires court approval, with a copy recorded with the county clerk for a homestead. An affidavit of heirship is a sworn statement filed with the clerk, but no law forces a title company to accept it.

  • Administered estate: an executor's or administrator's deed.
  • Will without administration: a court order and the will.
  • Transfer on death deed: an affidavit of death and a death certificate recorded.
  • No court action: an affidavit of heirship, which a buyer may question.

The county cannot add heirs to the old deed. A new instrument gets recorded instead.

sections.h2: How do foreclosure and tax liens appear in Washington County records?
sections.html:
A foreclosure sale notice has to be posted at the courthouse door and filed with the county clerk at least 21 days before the sale, and the clerk's page lists posted foreclosure notices. A buyer or seller can check those postings for a house that is behind on its loan.

Texas sales happen at a public auction between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. on the first Tuesday of a month, in the area the commissioners court has designated for the county and recorded in the real property records. A borrower generally has 20 days from the notice of default to reinstate. State tax liens are different. The Comptroller files notice with the county clerk, who records it in the state tax lien book, and a federal tax lien recorded with the clerk draws the $30.00 fee shown above.

Property tax liens attach on January 1 each year and do not appear as recorded deeds. Ask the Washington County tax office for a tax certificate before closing, and note that the clerk requires one for a plat.

sections.h2: What should a Washington County seller check before closing?
sections.html:
Pull the deed and every recorded lien for the address, and confirm that every release has been filed. A title company will do the same, but finding a gap early saves time.

  • Search the online index for the current deed, deeds of trust, releases and affidavits.
  • Confirm that the owner on the deed matches the person selling, or record the heirship instrument first.
  • Ask the county for a tax certificate and pay delinquent taxes from proceeds if needed.
  • Look for a posted foreclosure notice if a payment has been missed.
  • Check a plat if the lot was recently divided.

Recorded documents are public, so a buyer's title company will see everything on the record for the property.

faqs.q: Which office takes deeds for recording in Washington County, Texas?
faqs.a: At the Washington County Clerk, 100 East Main Street, Suite 102, Brenham, TX 77833. Mailed documents need the original signed deed and the filing fee, and the clerk's page lists a $25.00 first-page fee and $4.00 per added page.

faqs.q: Can I search Washington County deed records online?
faqs.a: Yes. The clerk's page says official public records are available online through eDocTec, covering deed records and official public records from 1836 to the present.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee for a plat?
faqs.a: The county lists $70.00 per slide to file a plat and $10.00 for a copy. A plat needs a tax certificate showing no delinquent ad valorem taxes, among other items.

faqs.q: Does Washington County record transfer on death deeds?
faqs.a: The county clerk is the recorder for deeds in the county. Under the state's guidance a transfer on death deed must be recorded with the clerk of the land's county before the owner's death to take effect.

faqs.q: Who do I call at the clerk's office?
faqs.a: The clerk's page lists 979-277-6216 for marriage license appointments, and that is the number to try for questions about the office. Ask about hours and recording in the same call.
